text:
ConocoPhillips fell 3.9% today as crude oil prices dropped sharply on hopes that the U.S. and Iran might pursue a diplomatic settlement rather than escalating military conflict in the Middle East. Oil companies like ConocoPhillips benefit when crude prices are high—lower oil prices directly reduce their production revenue and profit margins. The sharp decline follows the stock's strong run last Friday (up to $154), suggesting investors are repricing their bets on how high energy prices will stay.

The broader context here is that oil prices remain caught between conflicting pressures: geopolitical tensions that normally push prices up, versus peace-talk headlines and political pledges to bring energy costs down that pull prices lower. The gap between U.S. crude ($103/barrel) and world crude ($123/barrel) shows that global supply concerns are still elevated, but the momentum today clearly favored the diplomatic-resolution narrative over the conflict-premium scenario.
